Genotype-by-environment means

Source: R/ge_mean.R
ge_mean.Rd

ge_mean() computes the table of genotype-by-environment cell means and the grand mean, the data of the AMMI model.

Usage

ge_mean(.data, .y, .gen, .env)

# Default S3 method
ge_mean(.data, .y, .gen, .env)

Arguments

.data

a data frame with one row per plot.

.y, .gen, .env

the columns of the response, genotypes and environments: bare names, strings or vectors.

Value

A list (class c("bam_ge_mean", "bam_result", "list")) with ge_means, the \(G \times E\) matrix of means (row and column names: genotypes and environments), and grand_mean.

Details

With \(y_{ijl}\) the response of genotype \(i\) in replicate \(l\) of environment \(j\) and \(n_{ij}\) the number of replicates of the cell, $$\bar{y}_{ij} = \frac{1}{n_{ij}}\sum_l y_{ijl}, \qquad \bar{y} = \frac{1}{GE}\sum_{ij}\bar{y}_{ij}.$$ Genotypes and environments are in the order of their factor levels (sorted values when the columns are not factors).

References

Crossa, J., Perez-Elizalde, S., Jarquin, D., Cotes, J. M., Viele, K., Liu, G. and Cornelius, P. L. (2011). Bayesian estimation of the additive main effects and multiplicative interaction model. \emphCrop Science, \strong51(4), 1458–1469. \doi10.2135/cropsci2010.06.0343

See also

ge_var, ge_eff, ge_ammi

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

data(Maiz)
ge_mean(
    .data = Maiz
  , .y    = y
  , .gen  = entry
  , .env  = site
  )
